subject: POC trial plan & model selection for Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@acme.com>, Tom Ellis <tom@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial plan & model selection for Acme - follow up from discovery

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great to learn more about Acme's search assistant goals and the constraints around latency and multilingual support. As promised, here's a suggested POC/trial plan and proposed model selection so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and ownership.

1) Success criteria (what we need to validate)
- Retrieval + generation intent accuracy: intent classification/top-1 intent match >= 90% on your test set.
- Hallucination: < 2% rate on the sampled queries.
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 200ms for 512-token window, with a throughput baseline of ~30 reqs/s.
- Cost: target inference cost <= $0.00035/token (we'll provide estimated cost numbers per model).
- Multilingual: Spanish & French responses should meet the same accuracy thresholds for prioritized intents.

2) Proposed models for the trial (primary / fallback)
- Primary: Llama 2 13B (quantized) — best balance of quality and cost for your retrieval-augmented generation workload.
- Fallback: Llama 2 7B (quantized) — lower-cost alternative if we need lower memory footprint or faster cold-starts.
- Notes: If we see specific failure modes on multilingual prompts, we can try Mistral small/mix or a finetuned adapter as a secondary experiment.

3) Evaluation plan & datasets
- We'll run a 2-week blind evaluation with: (a) your curated test set of ~1k representative queries (please confirm), (b) a synthetic set we generate for edge cases, and (c) multilingual subsets for ES/FR.
- Metrics: top-1 accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, hallucination counts (human-annotated sample), latency P95, and per-token cost.
- Deliverables: daily run summary, final evaluation report, and recommended next-step model/profile.

4) Ownership and roles
- Redwood SE (Aditya) will own model runtime configuration and initial tuning.
- Acme: product owner for eval datasets + annotation support (Sara).
- Marissa (me): commercial owner — rollout decisions, procurement coordination, and executive updates.

5) Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): confirm datasets, success criteria, and kickoff date.
- Week 1: infra setup + baseline runs on Llama 2 13B.
- Week 2: blind eval & multilingual tests.
- End of Week 2 / Week 3: final report and decision call.

6) Next steps (action items)
- Sara: confirm the canonical test set (or share a sample) and any PII/redaction needs.
- Tom: confirm whether Acme prefers a hosted or VPC trial (impacts infra lead times).
- Aditya: will share a first-pass config + estimated cost for the two model options by EOD tomorrow.

I've attached a one-page POC plan and a small sample eval dataset to get started.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme_poc-plan.xlsx], [Attachment: acme_eval_dataset_sample.csv]

Thanks — excited to get this moving.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC trial plan & model selection for Acme - follow up from discovery

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and proposed plan. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications:

1) Dataset: I can share a 1k test set this afternoon. We do have PII in ~8% of records — we'll need redaction or a secure handling plan.
2) Hosted vs VPC: initial preference is VPC trial (we need to keep logs within our cloud account). Any lead time we should budget for?
3) Multilingual: Spanish is highest priority, French is second. We'll provide labels for both.

If you can get Aditya's config + cost estimates today, we can confirm kickoff for Monday (2026-06-22).

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Search Product — Acme Corp
Sara.Khan@acme.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@acme.com>, Tom Ellis <tom@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial plan & model selection for Acme - config + cost estimates

Sara / Tom —

Quick technical details and preliminary cost/infra notes based on Marissa's plan and your VPC preference.

1) Infra lead time for VPC trial
- Standard VPC deployment: 3–5 business days to provision and validate networking, KMS, and audit logging (we'll need your infra contacts for IAM roles and an allowlist).
- If you want a faster onsite-hosted proof (short-term), we can run a hosted trial while parallelizing VPC setup.

2) Model config (initial)
- Llama 2 13B, quantized int8, sequence length 1024, KV cache enabled, beam=1, sampling top_p=0.95 for generation.
- Fallback: Llama 2 7B, same quantization and profile (lower memory, lower cost).

3) Cost estimates (ballpark)
- Llama 2 13B (quantized): ~$0.00033 / token (inference only) at expected batching levels.
- Llama 2 7B (quantized): ~$0.00018 / token.
- Final numbers will depend on actual P95 latency targets and sustained throughput; we'll provide a refined estimate after baseline runs.

4) Multilingual notes
- Spanish and French: base Llama 2 models perform reasonably but we often see degradation on domain-specific terms. We recommend providing a small finetuning set (~200-500 labeled examples per language) or a retrieval-augmented setup with language-specific context.

5) Security/compliance
- Attached is our standard security questionnaire template. For VPC trials, we support customer-managed KMS and audit logging to meet your retention requirements.

Attachments: [Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf]

Action items I'll follow up on:
- Share exact infra checklist & IAM steps (today).
- Run quick baseline on Llama 2 13B and share preliminary latency + cost numbers by EOD tomorrow.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
